subject: OrchidAI commitment — tokens/sec modeling, latency slack & burst plan
messages:
From: Maria Vazquez <maria.vazquez@orchidai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: SLO Team <slo-team@orchidai.com>, Kenji Ito <k.ito@orchidai.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity planning ask: committed throughput + SLA alignment

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency guarantees and the autoscale behavior. We're getting internal buy-in to move from a POC to a 12‑month committed plan but need a few things from Redwood before we can finalize:

- A deal-specific tokens/sec estimate (avg and peak) mapped to a recommended Dedicated GPU commit.
- A short latency/SLO fit analysis (p50/p95 for our typical prompt mixes) and recommended headroom percentage for safety.
- Burst strategy for nightly model updates and weekly evaluation runs (how much temporary headroom do we need).

For context: OrchidAI's prod load today is about 18M prompt tokens/month and 120M generated tokens/month (approx 138M total tokens/month), with spikes tied to timezone-driven traffic windows. Typical concurrent requests during a peak minute hit ~320 active sessions; our app-level SLO is p95 < 160ms for single-turn text generation. We will be using a 13B dense model (quantized) for now.

I've attached a small traffic sample and a draft spreadsheet with our monthly token numbers. Can you propose a baseline commit (GPUs) and a plan for headroom + burst? We're hoping to finalize commercial terms by end of next week.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Vazquez
Head of Platform Engineering, OrchidAI
maria.vazquez@orchidai.com

Attachments: orchidai-traffic-sample-jan2027.csv, orchidai-commit-modeling-v1.xlsx

Cc: avery_johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity planning ask: committed throughput + SLA alignment

Hi Maria — thanks for the context and for attaching the sample. Forwarding to our infra and solutions leads; we can run a quick model-to-GPU mapping and come back with a conservative commit + a burst policy. A few clarifying Qs to help the sizing:

1) Typical sequence length (prompt + expected generation) median/95th? You gave tokens/month but distribution matters.
2) Are you planning many short synchronous calls (chat-like) or fewer long-generation jobs (single long responses)?
3) Will you want prefix caching across sessions (i.e., many users share similar prompts)?

If you can confirm the above today we'll aim to send a vendor-side modeling spreadsheet + recommended commit options (conservative / aggressive) by EOD Friday.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity planning ask: committed throughput + SLA alignment

Hi all — dug into the traffic sample and the draft spreadsheet. Below is our modeling summary and recommended commit. I'm including assumptions up front.

Assumptions:
- Model: 13B dense quantized (INT8-ish profile) — typical tokens/sec on A100-80GB equiv: 650–900 tokens/sec per GPU when run with batching tuned for short chat-like responses.
- Median sequence length: 160 tokens (prompt+gen) from your sample; p95 sequence length: ~520 tokens.
- Typical request shape: majority synchronous chat-like calls; average generation portion ~110 tokens.
- We size for p95 SLO < 160ms (app-level) but include runtime overhead (network, routing) budget of ~40ms, so target runtime p95 ~120ms.

Raw throughput mapping (approx):
- Single GPU sustained: ~750 tokens/sec (middle of range) at modest batching (batch size ~8–16 depending on concurrency).
- Concurrency behavior: with continuous batching, effective user-facing latency stays low until GPU slot saturation; beyond that latency increases non-linearly.

Projected demand:
- Current baseline tokens/month (138M) ≈ average 53.1 tokens/sec sustained across the month.
- Peak window (timezone spikes) from your sample maps to ~2.1x baseline → peak sustained ~112 tokens/sec.
- Peak-minute concurrency (320 active sessions), with 110 gen tokens per request and average think-time, maps to instantaneous token-in-flight demand ~620 tokens/sec.

Recommendation (commit + headroom):
- Baseline committed capacity: 1 x A100-class GPU (equivalent) covers baseline sustained needs with modest autoscale; however this offers little headroom for peaks.
- Recommended committed pool for reliable p95 < 160ms in peak windows: 2 x A100-class GPUs (equiv) dedicated to your model, with autoscale burst to 4 GPUs for short windows. This provides ~1.5–2x headroom vs observed peaks and keeps p95 compute runtime ~90–110ms (giving network/routing slack).
- Headroom: target 50–100% compute headroom on committed capacity depending on your tolerance for cold-start/autoscale latency. We recommend 75% as sweet spot for OrchidAI.

Burst strategy for maintenance/evals:
- Nightly model updates / eval runs: schedule as low-priority jobs on burst pool; recommend temporary burst to +2 GPUs (on top of the 4) for 30–90 minute windows during off-peak.
- Use prefix/KV caching for common prompt families to shave 15–25% of token work during user peaks.

Latency estimates (runtime-only, p50/p95) for recommended commit (2 GPU committed, burst to 4):
- p50 runtime: ~45–60ms
- p95 runtime: ~90–110ms
- With network/routing budget + infra overhead, Orchids' app-level p95 target ~160ms remains achievable with the recommended commit and 75% headroom.

Costs & ops notes:
- If you want a lower committed spend, 1 GPU commit + larger autoscale (burst to 5–6 GPUs) is possible but increases exposure to autoscale latency during sharp spikes.
- We'll provide a spreadsheet mapping tokens/sec scenarios to GPUs per hour and expected monthly spend for each commit tier.

I've attached a first-pass XLS with scenario tabs. Happy to walk through in a quick call.

- Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Capacity planning ask: committed throughput + SLA alignment

Maria — putting commercial recommendations on top of Aditya's technical write-up.

Options (12‑month term):
1) Conservative (recommended for reliability):
   - Commit: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool)
   - Burst: autoscale up to 4 GPUs (per Aditya's runbook)
   - Headroom: ~75% target
   - Monthly committed spend: USD 38,400
   - Estimated monthly overage budget (if fully used bursts): USD 4,200

2) Cost-first (saves CAPEX but higher autoscale risk):
   - Commit: 1 x A100-equivalent GPU
   - Burst: autoscale to 5 GPUs when needed
   - Headroom: lower, ~30–40% on commit; rely on autoscale for spikes
   - Monthly committed spend: USD 21,600
   - Estimated monthly overage budget: USD 9,800

Notes & next steps:
- The conservative plan (2 GPUs) aligns with your p95 < 160ms target with small operational risk and gives predictable billing.
- We'll include a canary rollout schedule in the contract so you can validate p95 in production before full traffic cutover.
- I can get legal to prepare a term sheet and a DocuSign link if you confirm which option you prefer.

If helpful, we can run a 30‑minute sizing walkthrough on Thursday.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — that all looks sensible and aligns with our internal modeling. We'll proceed with Option 1 (2 GPU commit, burst to 4) pending final term sheet. A few final items before I sign:

- Can you add a line to the term sheet for a monthly 90‑minute scheduled evaluation window where we can burst +2 GPUs without additional charge? We run heavy weekly evaluation jobs and it would help with predictability.
- Please include a clause for a 14‑day canary period with the ability to dial up traffic gradually and validate p95 in prod.
- We prefer the billing cadence to be monthly with clear overage reporting and token-metering exported into our billing dashboard.

If you can send the DocuSign link with those three items included, I'll route it for signature on our side today.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maria
Maria Vazquez
Head of Platform Engineering, OrchidAI
